claim: P bodies are archetypal biomolecular condensates that concentrate proteins and RNA without a surrounding membrane.
source: P bodies are archetypal biomolecular condensates that concentrate proteins and RNA without a surrounding membrane.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about P bodies that is part of established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Only seven proteins are highly concentrated in yeast P bodies at concentrations of 5.1–15µM.
source: Only seven proteins are highly concentrated in P bodies (5.1–15µM); the 24 others examined are appreciably lower (most ≤ 2.6µM).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements of protein concentrations in P bodies presented in the manuscript.

claim: 24 P body proteins examined have concentrations appreciably lower than highly concentrated proteins, with most at or below 2.6µM.
source: Only seven proteins are highly concentrated in P bodies (5.1–15µM); the 24 others examined are appreciably lower (most ≤ 2.6µM).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements of protein concentrations in P bodies presented in the manuscript.

claim: P body concentration correlates inversely with cytoplasmic exchange rate.
source: P body concentration correlates inversely with cytoplasmic exchange rate.
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP measurements and concentration data showing the relationship between these parameters.

claim: Sequence elements driving Dcp2 concentration into P bodies are distributed across the protein.
source: Sequence elements driving Dcp2 concentration into P bodies are distributed across the protein and act synergistically.
evidence: This claim is supported by experiments with various Dcp2 deletion and mutation constructs showing contributions from multiple regions.

claim: Sequence elements driving Dcp2 concentration into P bodies act synergistically.
source: Sequence elements driving Dcp2 concentration into P bodies are distributed across the protein and act synergistically.
evidence: This claim is supported by experiments showing that combined elements produce greater partitioning than expected from individual contributions.

claim: P bodies and probably other condensates are compositionally simpler than suggested by proteomic analyses.
source: Our data indicate that P bodies, and probably other condensates, are compositionally simpler than suggested by proteomic analyses, with implications for specificity, reconstitution and evolution.
evidence: This claim is based on the quantitative data showing only a small number of highly concentrated proteins, combined with inference about other condensates.

claim: Eukaryotic cells contain numerous compartments that concentrate specific sets of molecules without a surrounding membrane.
source: Eukaryotic cells contain numerous compartments that concentrate specific sets of molecules without a surrounding membrane (Banani et al., 2017; Shin and Brangwynne, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature establishing this concept.

claim: Biomolecular condensates are related to a variety of biological processes.
source: These structures, referred to as biomolecular condensates, are related to a variety of biological processes.
evidence: This is a general statement supported by the examples that follow in the text and established scientific knowledge.

claim: P bodies are associated with RNA metabolism.
source: Examples include cytoplasmic processing bodies (P bodies) associated with RNA metabolism (Decker and Parker, 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: PML NBs are involved in transcription, DNA damage repair, and anti-viral responses.
source: promyelocytic leukemia nuclear bodies (PML NBs) involved in transcription, DNA damage repair, and anti-viral responses (Lallemand-Breitenbach and de Thé, 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Signaling clusters are involved in T cell activation.
source: signaling clusters in T cell activation (Su et al., 2016)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: HP1 clusters are involved in heterochromatin organization.
source: HP1 clusters in heterochromatin organization (Larson et al., 2017; Strom et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Many condensates form through self-assembly of multivalent molecules, including proteins composed of folded domains and/or disordered regions, RNA and DNA, and chromatin.
source: Many condensates form through self-assembly of multivalent molecules, including proteins composed of folded domains and/or disordered regions, RNA and DNA, and chromatin (Li et al., 2012; Kato et al., 2012; Nott et al., 2015; Su et al., 2016; Banani et al., 2017; Gibson et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Condensate self-assembly can lead to both liquid-like and solid-like structures.
source: This process can lead to both liquid-like and solid-like structures (Banani et al., 2017; Shin and Brangwynne, 2017; Alberti and Dormann, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Some condensates respond sharply to changes in concentration of key components or regulators, salt and/or temperature.
source: Some condensates have been shown to respond sharply to changes in concentration of key components or regulators, salt and/or temperature, suggesting that they form through highly cooperative assembly mechanisms, including phase transitions (Beutel et al., 2019; Brangwynne et al., 2009; Falahati and Wieschaus, 2017; Li et al., 2012; Riback et al., 2017; Saha et al., 2016; Smith et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2014; Weber and Brangwynne, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Sharp responses of condensates to environmental changes suggest they form through highly cooperative assembly mechanisms, including phase transitions.
source: Some condensates have been shown to respond sharply to changes in concentration of key components or regulators, salt and/or temperature, suggesting that they form through highly cooperative assembly mechanisms, including phase transitions (Beutel et al., 2019; Brangwynne et al., 2009; Falahati and Wieschaus, 2017; Li et al., 2012; Riback et al., 2017; Saha et al., 2016; Smith et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2014; Weber and Brangwynne, 2015).
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observed sharp responses, supported by citations.

claim: The activities of biomolecular condensates are thought to derive from the assembly of specific collections of functionally related molecules into a unique physical environment.
source: The activities of biomolecular condensates are thought to derive from the assembly of specific collections of functionally related molecules into a unique physical environment.
evidence: This is a theoretical statement representing current thinking in the field.

claim: Understanding condensates as chemical entities requires knowledge and understanding of their compositions.
source: Thus, understanding condensates as chemical entities requires knowledge and understanding of their compositions.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the previous statement about how condensate activities derive from their composition.

claim: Large-scale proteomics studies have been performed to determine comprehensive inventories of molecules that localize to stress granules.
source: Large-scale proteomics studies have been performed to determine comprehensive inventories of molecules that localize to different condensates, including stress granules (Jain et al., 2016; Markmiller et al., 2018; Youn et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous proteomic studies.

claim: Large-scale proteomics studies have been performed to determine comprehensive inventories of molecules that localize to P bodies.
source: Large-scale proteomics studies have been performed to determine comprehensive inventories of molecules that localize to different condensates, including stress granules (Jain et al., 2016; Markmiller et al., 2018; Youn et al., 2018), P bodies (Hubstenberger et al., 2017; Youn et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous proteomic studies.

claim: Large-scale proteomics studies have been performed to determine comprehensive inventories of molecules that localize to nucleoli.
source: Large-scale proteomics studies have been performed to determine comprehensive inventories of molecules that localize to different condensates, including stress granules (Jain et al., 2016; Markmiller et al., 2018; Youn et al., 2018), P bodies (Hubstenberger et al., 2017; Youn et al., 2018), and nucleoli (Andersen et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous proteomic study.

claim: Proteomic and localization studies suggest that condensates are biochemically complex, containing tens to hundreds of types of proteins and RNAs.
source: Cumulatively, these studies suggest that condensates are biochemically complex, containing tens to hundreds of types of proteins and RNAs that show dense and complex patterns of molecular interactions.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the cumulative results of proteomic and localization studies cited earlier.

claim: Condensate components show dense and complex patterns of molecular interactions.
source: Cumulatively, these studies suggest that condensates are biochemically complex, containing tens to hundreds of types of proteins and RNAs that show dense and complex patterns of molecular interactions.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the cumulative results of proteomic and localization studies.

claim: Some transcriptomic studies have been quantitative.
source: Although some transcriptomic studies and a few analyses of individual proteins have been quantitative (Khong et al., 2017; Klingauf et al., 2006; Leung et al., 2006; Wheeler et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous quantitative studies.

claim: A few analyses of individual proteins in condensates have been quantitative.
source: Although some transcriptomic studies and a few analyses of individual proteins have been quantitative (Khong et al., 2017; Klingauf et al., 2006; Leung et al., 2006; Wheeler et al., 2017)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous quantitative studies.

claim: Proteomic studies of condensates to date have been only qualitative.
source: Although some transcriptomic studies and a few analyses of individual proteins have been quantitative (Khong et al., 2017; Klingauf et al., 2006; Leung et al., 2006; Wheeler et al., 2017), proteomic studies to date have been only qualitative.
evidence: This claim is based on assessment of the existing proteomic literature.

claim: The relative and absolute concentrations of proteins in condensates are largely unknown.
source: Therefore, both the relative and absolute concentrations of proteins in condensates, and their relationships to molecular connectivity, are largely unknown.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the lack of quantitative proteomic studies.

claim: The relationships between protein concentrations in condensates and molecular connectivity are largely unknown.
source: Therefore, both the relative and absolute concentrations of proteins in condensates, and their relationships to molecular connectivity, are largely unknown.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the lack of quantitative studies.

claim: The relationships between concentration and dynamics of molecules in condensates have not been systematically explored.
source: Additionally, the relationships between concentration and dynamics of molecules in condensates have not been systematically explored.
evidence: This claim is based on assessment of the existing literature.

claim: Some condensate components are shared between different condensates.
source: Moreover, while some components are shared between different condensates, many are uniquely concentrated in specific condensates.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: Many condensate components are uniquely concentrated in specific condensates.
source: Moreover, while some components are shared between different condensates, many are uniquely concentrated in specific condensates.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: It is unclear how substantial specificity of condensate composition is determined in vivo.
source: It is still unclear how the substantial specificity is determined in vivo.
evidence: This identifies a gap in current understanding.

claim: P bodies are protein- and mRNA-rich cytoplasmic condensates conserved from yeast to mammals.
source: P bodies are protein- and mRNA-rich cytoplasmic condensates conserved from yeast to mammals (Ingelfinger et al., 2002; Sheth and Parker, 2003; van Dijk et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature establishing P body conservation.

claim: P bodies are thought to participate in RNA metabolism, modulating mRNA decay.
source: They are thought to participate in RNA metabolism, modulating mRNA decay and acting as sites of RNA storage during cellular stress (Aizer et al., 2014; Bhattacharyya et al., 2006; Cougot et al., 2004; Sheth and Parker, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: P bodies act as sites of RNA storage during cellular stress.
source: They are thought to participate in RNA metabolism, modulating mRNA decay and acting as sites of RNA storage during cellular stress (Aizer et al., 2014; Bhattacharyya et al., 2006; Cougot et al., 2004; Sheth and Parker, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The authors used quantitative fluorescence microscopy to measure absolute concentrations of 31 P body resident proteins within P bodies and in the surrounding cytoplasm.
source: Taking advantage of an available yeast GFP library, we used quantitative fluorescence microscopy to measure the absolute concentrations of 31 P body resident proteins within the condensates and in the surrounding cytoplasm.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The authors measured dynamic properties of P body proteins using fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP).
source: We also measured their dynamic properties using fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, Xrn1, Lsm1, Dhh1, and Upf1 are highly concentrated in P bodies at 5.1–15 µM.
source: We find that P body proteins segregate into two groups based on their concentrations in P bodies and dynamics. Members of the first group (Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, Xrn1, Lsm1, Dhh1, Upf1) are highly concentrated in P bodies (5.1–15 µM) and exchange slowly with the cytoplasm.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements presented in the study.

claim: Highly concentrated P body proteins exchange slowly with the cytoplasm.
source: Members of the first group (Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, Xrn1, Lsm1, Dhh1, Upf1) are highly concentrated in P bodies (5.1–15 µM) and exchange slowly with the cytoplasm.
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP measurements presented in the study.

claim: All highly concentrated P body proteins except Xrn1 have high connectivity, interacting with multiple P body components.
source: Except for Xrn1, these all have high connectivity, interacting with multiple P body components.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of protein-protein interactions from the literature.

claim: Partitioning of Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, and Xrn1 into P bodies is correlated.
source: Partitioning of several of these highly concentrated (HC) proteins (Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, and Xrn1) into P bodies is correlated, suggesting that they assemble cooperatively, consistent with their high connectivity.
evidence: This claim is supported by measurements of paired protein concentrations in the same P bodies.

claim: Correlated partitioning of HC proteins suggests they assemble cooperatively.
source: Partitioning of several of these highly concentrated (HC) proteins (Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, and Xrn1) into P bodies is correlated, suggesting that they assemble cooperatively, consistent with their high connectivity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed correlation in partitioning.

claim: All proteins known to contribute strongly to P body formation through genetic studies are in the highly concentrated group.
source: All proteins known to contribute strongly to P body formation through genetic studies are in this HC group.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison with previous genetic studies in the literature.

claim: Less concentrated P body proteins are at substantially lower concentrations (0.7–2.6 µM except Sbp1).
source: In contrast, members of the second less concentrated (LC) group are at substantially lower concentrations in P bodies (all except Sbp1, 0.7–2.6 µM) and exhibit faster dynamics.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements presented in the study.

claim: Less concentrated P body proteins exhibit faster dynamics than highly concentrated proteins.
source: In contrast, members of the second less concentrated (LC) group are at substantially lower concentrations in P bodies (all except Sbp1, 0.7–2.6 µM) and exhibit faster dynamics.
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP measurements presented in the study.

claim: All less concentrated P body proteins have low connectivity.
source: These all have low connectivity.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of protein-protein interactions from the literature.

claim: The N-terminal domain of Dcp2 contributes to partitioning into P bodies.
source: In a molecular dissection of Dcp2, we find that the N-terminal domain, multivalent C-terminal domain, and central high affinity Edc3 binding site all contribute to partitioning of the protein into P bodies and to its dynamic exchange with the cytoplasm.
evidence: This claim is supported by experiments with Dcp2 deletion constructs.

claim: The multivalent C-terminal domain of Dcp2 contributes to partitioning into P bodies.
source: In a molecular dissection of Dcp2, we find that the N-terminal domain, multivalent C-terminal domain, and central high affinity Edc3 binding site all contribute to partitioning of the protein into P bodies and to its dynamic exchange with the cytoplasm.
evidence: This claim is supported by experiments with Dcp2 deletion constructs.

claim: The central high affinity Edc3 binding site of Dcp2 contributes to partitioning into P bodies.
source: In a molecular dissection of Dcp2, we find that the N-terminal domain, multivalent C-terminal domain, and central high affinity Edc3 binding site all contribute to partitioning of the protein into P bodies and to its dynamic exchange with the cytoplasm.
evidence: This claim is supported by experiments with Dcp2 deletion constructs.

claim: The N-terminal and C-terminal domains of Dcp2 can act synergistically to promote recruitment into P bodies.
source: Moreover, the N-terminal and C-terminal domains can act synergistically to promote recruitment of Dcp2 into P bodies.
evidence: This claim is supported by experiments showing greater than additive effects when domains are combined.

claim: The highly distributive organization of Dcp2 recruitment elements suggests a ready means of quantitatively modulating condensate composition during evolution.
source: This highly distributive organization suggests a ready means of quantitatively modulating condensate composition during evolution.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about evolutionary implications based on the observed organization.

claim: While a condensate may contain many components, only a small number are highly concentrated there.
source: These data suggest that while a condensate may contain many components, only a small number are highly concentrated there.
evidence: This is a generalization based on the quantitative data from P bodies.

claim: P bodies in wild type S. cerevisiae are typically diffraction-limited in size under normal conditions.
source: P bodies in wild type S. cerevisiae are typically diffraction-limited in size under normal conditions.
evidence: This is an observation based on microscopy of wild type cells.

claim: P bodies become larger when mRNA decay is decreased.
source: But they become larger when mRNA decay is decreased, for example when mRNA decay proteins such as Dcp1 are deleted or when cells respond to stresses such as glucose starvation (Teixeira et al., 2005; Teixeira and Parker, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and observations in this study.

claim: P bodies become larger when Dcp1 is deleted.
source: But they become larger when mRNA decay is decreased, for example when mRNA decay proteins such as Dcp1 are deleted or when cells respond to stresses such as glucose starvation (Teixeira et al., 2005; Teixeira and Parker, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and observations in this study.

claim: P bodies become larger when cells respond to glucose starvation.
source: But they become larger when mRNA decay is decreased, for example when mRNA decay proteins such as Dcp1 are deleted or when cells respond to stresses such as glucose starvation (Teixeira et al., 2005; Teixeira and Parker, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and observations in this study.

claim: The authors analyzed GFP-tagged proteins expressed in a dcp1Δ strain.
source: Initially we analyzed GFP-tagged proteins expressed in a dcp1Δ strain, because the effects of stress are time-dependent and thus more difficult to perform systematically measurements across a series of strains.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The authors individually expressed 31 reported P body resident proteins tagged with GFP at their C-termini in their chromosomal location under their endogenous promoters.
source: We individually expressed 31 reported P body resident proteins tagged with GFP at their C-termini in their chromosomal location under their endogenous promoters (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The GFP-tagged proteins co-localize with mCherry-tagged Edc3, a P body marker.
source: We presume these puncta are P bodies because previous reports that the proteins localize to P bodies and in all cases tested we observed co-localization of the proteins with an mCherry-tagged P body marker, Edc3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The authors limited analyses to P bodies larger than the x-y PSF of the microscope.
source: Using confocal microscopy, we limited our analyses to P bodies that were larger than the x-y PSF of our microscope (see Materials and methods), and corrected the diluting effect of the larger z-PSF based on an assumption that the structures were spherical.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach used in the study.

claim: The authors corrected for the diluting effect of the z-PSF based on an assumption that P bodies are spherical.
source: Using confocal microscopy, we limited our analyses to P bodies that were larger than the x-y PSF of our microscope (see Materials and methods), and corrected the diluting effect of the larger z-PSF based on an assumption that the structures were spherical.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach used in the study.

claim: The partition coefficient is calculated as the ratio of P body concentration to cytoplasmic concentration.
source: We calculated the partition coefficient (PC) as the ratio of these two values.
evidence: This describes the definition of partition coefficient used in the study.

claim: Of the 31 proteins analyzed, 19 showed sufficiently punctate distributions in mid-log phase to permit analysis (PC >~2).
source: Of the 31 proteins, 19 showed sufficiently punctate distributions in mid-log phase to permit analysis (PC >~2).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental analysis.

claim: 12 proteins were distributed relatively uniformly in the cytoplasm and their P body concentrations could not be analyzed.
source: The remaining 12 proteins were distributed relatively uniformly in the cytoplasm and their P body concentrations could not be analyzed; these may be stress or strain specific proteins that do not concentrate in P bodies under our experimental conditions (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental analysis.

claim: The 12 uniformly distributed proteins may be stress or strain specific proteins that do not concentrate in P bodies under the experimental conditions used.
source: The remaining 12 proteins were distributed relatively uniformly in the cytoplasm and their P body concentrations could not be analyzed; these may be stress or strain specific proteins that do not concentrate in P bodies under our experimental conditions (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observation.

claim: The PC values and dynamics of Edc3 tagged with GFP and mCherry are similar.
source: First, the PC values and dynamics of Edc3 and Dhh1 tagged with GFP and mCherry were similar (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: The PC values and dynamics of Dhh1 tagged with GFP and mCherry are similar.
source: First, the PC values and dynamics of Edc3 and Dhh1 tagged with GFP and mCherry were similar (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: The PC values and dynamics of Dcp2 are nearly identical with an N-terminal or C-terminal GFP tag.
source: Second, the PC values and dynamics of Dcp2 are nearly identical with an N-terminal or C-terminal GFP tag (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The GFP tag probably does not strongly affect protein behaviors.
source: Two observations suggest that the GFP tag probably does not strongly affect protein behaviors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similar behaviors observed with different tags and tag positions.

claim: It remains possible that some proteins are affected by the GFP tag.
source: It remains possible that some other proteins are affected by the tag.
evidence: This acknowledges a limitation of the study.

claim: Average PC values of the 19 regular P body proteins range from a maximum of 133 (Dcp2) to a minimum of ~5 (Eap1, Ssd1).
source: Average PC values of the 19 regular P body proteins had a wide range, with a maximum of 133 (Dcp2) steadily decreasing to a minimum of ~5 (Eap1, Ssd1) (Figure 1A and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and Supplementary file 2.

claim: Only a few proteins have high partition coefficients, including Dcp2 (133 ± 13), Edc3 (133 ± 8) and Pat1 (107 ± 12).
source: Only a few proteins had high partition coefficients, including Dcp2 (133 ± 13), Edc3 (133 ± 8) and Pat1 (107 ± 12); the majority had PC values < 20.
evidence: This claim is supported by the quantitative measurements presented in the study.

claim: The majority of regular P body proteins have PC values < 20.
source: Only a few proteins had high partition coefficients, including Dcp2 (133 ± 13), Edc3 (133 ± 8) and Pat1 (107 ± 12); the majority had PC values < 20.
evidence: This claim is supported by the quantitative measurements presented in the study.

claim: Absolute concentrations of proteins in P bodies range from ~0.7 µM to 15 µM.
source: We also obtained absolute concentrations of each protein in P bodies, which ranged from ~0.7 µM to 15 µM and revealed two notable features of P bodies.
evidence: This claim is supported by the quantitative measurements presented in the study.

claim: Seven proteins (Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, Xrn1, Lsm1, Dhh1 and Upf1) have average P body concentrations of 8.9–12 µM.
source: First, seven proteins, Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, Xrn1, Lsm1 (likely representing the entire, constitutive Lsm1-7 assembly [Sharif and Conti, 2013]), Dhh1 and Upf1 – had average P body concentrations of 8.9–12 µM, with a slightly higher concentration (15 µM) for Dcp2 and slightly lower concentration (5 µM) for Upf1.
evidence: This claim is supported by the quantitative measurements presented in the study.

claim: Dcp2 has a P body concentration of 15 µM.
source: First, seven proteins, Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, Xrn1, Lsm1 (likely representing the entire, constitutive Lsm1-7 assembly [Sharif and Conti, 2013]), Dhh1 and Upf1 – had average P body concentrations of 8.9–12 µM, with a slightly higher concentration (15 µM) for Dcp2 and slightly lower concentration (5 µM) for Upf1.
evidence: This claim is supported by the quantitative measurements presented in the study.

claim: Upf1 has a P body concentration of 5 µM.
source: First, seven proteins, Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, Xrn1, Lsm1 (likely representing the entire, constitutive Lsm1-7 assembly [Sharif and Conti, 2013]), Dhh1 and Upf1 – had average P body concentrations of 8.9–12 µM, with a slightly higher concentration (15 µM) for Dcp2 and slightly lower concentration (5 µM) for Upf1.
evidence: This claim is supported by the quantitative measurements presented in the study.

claim: Lsm1 likely represents the entire, constitutive Lsm1-7 assembly.
source: First, seven proteins, Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, Xrn1, Lsm1 (likely representing the entire, constitutive Lsm1-7 assembly [Sharif and Conti, 2013]), Dhh1 and Upf1 – had average P body concentrations of 8.9–12 µM, with a slightly higher concentration (15 µM) for Dcp2 and slightly lower concentration (5 µM) for Upf1.
evidence: This is an inference based on citation to previous literature about the Lsm1-7 complex.

claim: There is a clear, sharp distinction between highly concentrated (HC) and less concentrated (LC) proteins in P bodies.
source: A second striking observation was that there was a clear, sharp distinction between highly concentrated (HC) and less concentrated (LC) proteins (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the concentration data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: After the HC proteins, most other proteins have P body concentrations < 2.6 µM, with most ~1 µM.
source: After the HC proteins most other proteins have P body concentrations < 2.6 µM, with most ~1 µM.
evidence: This claim is supported by the quantitative measurements presented in the study.

claim: Sbp1 has a P body concentration of 4.6 µM.
source: The only exception is Sbp1 (4.6 µM), which also has a very high cytoplasmic concentration, affording it a high P body concentration even with a small PC value (Figure 1, and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the quantitative measurements presented in the study.

claim: Sbp1 has a very high cytoplasmic concentration.
source: The only exception is Sbp1 (4.6 µM), which also has a very high cytoplasmic concentration, affording it a high P body concentration even with a small PC value (Figure 1, and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the quantitative measurements presented in the study.

claim: Sbp1 is not highly enriched in glucose-starved wild type P bodies.
source: Sbp1 also is not highly enriched in glucose-starved wild type P bodies (see below); for these reasons we do not include it in the HC group.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented later in the manuscript.

claim: The total cellular concentrations measured in this study are similar to a unified quantitative protein abundance database of S. cerevisiae.
source: Our data are consistent with previously reported measurements since the total cellular concentrations that we measured are similar to a unified quantitative protein abundance database of S. cerevisiae (Ho et al., 2018; Figure 1—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison with published data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3D.

claim: Yeast P bodies contain many different proteins, but only a relatively small number are highly concentrated in the compartment.
source: Together, these data show that while yeast P bodies can contain many different proteins, only a relatively small number are highly concentrated in the compartment, and the majority of components are weakly concentrated.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the quantitative data presented.

claim: The majority of P body components are weakly concentrated.
source: Together, these data show that while yeast P bodies can contain many different proteins, only a relatively small number are highly concentrated in the compartment, and the majority of components are weakly concentrated.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the quantitative data presented.

claim: Regular P body proteins exchange with the cytoplasm with very different rates and fractional recoveries.
source: This analysis revealed that the regular P body proteins exchange with the cytoplasm with very different rates and fractional recoveries (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dcp2 and Edc3 show no measurable recovery on a 150 s timescale.
source: At one end of the distribution, Dcp2 and Edc3 showed no measurable recovery on a 150 s timescale.
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP measurements presented in the study.

claim: Pat1 and Upf1 show intermediate rates and extents of recovery (k = ~0.01 s−1, recovery = ~50%).
source: Proteins such as Pat1 and Upf1, showed intermediate rates and extents of recovery (k = ~0.01 s−1, recovery = ~50%).
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP measurements presented in the study.

claim: Sbp1 and Eap1 recover nearly 100% in 150 s (k = 0.07 s−1).
source: While at the other end of the spectrum, proteins such as Sbp1 and Eap1 recovered nearly 100% in 150 s (k = 0.07 s−1).
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP measurements presented in the study.

claim: HC proteins tend to have slower exchange rates and less fractional recoveries than LC proteins.
source: Although exchange rate and recovery for both the HC proteins and LC proteins spanned broad ranges, the former (Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, Xrn1, Lsm1, Upf1, and Dhh1) tended to have slower exchange rates and less fractional recoveries than the latter (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 2.

claim: For the HC group, the exchange rate is on average five-fold smaller than the LC group.
source: On average, for the HC group, the exchange rate was five-fold smaller than the LC group, and recovery fraction was two-fold lower (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 2.

claim: For the HC group, the recovery fraction is on average two-fold lower than the LC group.
source: On average, for the HC group, the exchange rate was five-fold smaller than the LC group, and recovery fraction was two-fold lower (Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The slower recovery dynamics of HC proteins are not simply due to smaller fluorescent pools in cytoplasm.
source: Three observations argue that the slower recovery dynamics of the HC proteins are not simply due to smaller fluorescent pools in cytoplasm, but rather reflect different interactions in the P body.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple lines of evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: Neither exchange rate nor fractional recovery correlates with protein concentrations in cytoplasm.
source: First, neither exchange rate nor fractional recovery correlates with protein concentrations in cytoplasm (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: Less than 50% of the total pool of each protein is localized to the P body (<8% for most).

evidence: This is a theoretical prediction based on principles of multivalent interactions.

claim: Many of the LC components are RNA binding proteins.
source: Since many of the LC components are RNA binding proteins (Supplementary file 3 and Figure 2—figure supplement 4), we suggest they are recruited into P bodies by the high local concentration of RNA.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of protein properties from the literature.

claim: LC components are recruited into P bodies by the high local concentration of RNA.
source: Since many of the LC components are RNA binding proteins (Supplementary file 3 and Figure 2—figure supplement 4), we suggest they are recruited into P bodies by the high local concentration of RNA.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the RNA binding properties of LC proteins.

claim: The LC components with the highest PC (Pop2, Ccr4, Upf2, Upf3) all have direct interactions with a HC P body component.
source: The LC components with the highest PC (Pop2, Ccr4, Upf2, Upf3) all also have direct interactions with a HC P body component (Pop2 interacting with Dhh1, Upf2 interacting with Upf1)
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of protein-protein interactions from the literature.

claim: Partitioning is determined by cooperative interactions of a given protein with multiple components within a condensate.
source: The LC components with the highest PC (Pop2, Ccr4, Upf2, Upf3) all also have direct interactions with a HC P body component (Pop2 interacting with Dhh1, Upf2 interacting with Upf1), consistent with the idea that partitioning is determined by cooperative interactions of a given protein with multiple components within a condensate (see below).
evidence: This is a general principle inferred from the observations.

claim: Connectivity and its molecular underpinning, valency of interaction, is likely to provide significant predictive power in understanding the composition of condensates.
source: Thus, connectivity, and its molecular underpinning, valency of interaction, is likely to provide significant predictive power in understanding the composition of condensates.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of connectivity as a predictive parameter.

claim: While connectivity is significantly correlated with P body concentration and dynamics, the correlation is not perfect.
source: We note that while connectivity is significantly correlated with P body concentration and dynamics, the correlation is not perfect, likely because affinity and energy-consuming processes, in addition to connectivity, can play a significant role.
evidence: This acknowledges limitations of connectivity as a sole predictor.

claim: Affinity and energy-consuming processes, in addition to connectivity, can play a significant role in determining P body concentration and dynamics.
source: We note that while connectivity is significantly correlated with P body concentration and dynamics, the correlation is not perfect, likely because affinity and energy-consuming processes, in addition to connectivity, can play a significant role.
evidence: This is an inference about factors affecting partitioning beyond connectivity.

claim: The PC of the 1–300 fragment of Dcp2, which includes the HLM1 high affinity binding site for Edc3, is 132.
source: For example, the PC of the 1–300 fragment of Dcp2, which includes the HLM1 high affinity binding site for Edc3, is 132.
evidence: This is a specific example illustrating the role of high affinity interactions.

claim: The PC of Dcp2∆H1 ∆5H, where HLM1 is replaced by lower affinity binding sites for Edc3, is only 31.
source: In contrast, the PC of the Dcp2∆H1 ∆5H, where HLM1 is replaced by lower affinity binding sites for Edc3 in the C terminal extension of Dcp2, is only 31.
evidence: This is a specific example illustrating the role of affinity in partitioning.

claim: Xrn1 is concentrated in P bodies to ~10 µM even though it only has two connections to other P body components.
source: Similarly, the HC protein Xrn1 is concentrated in P bodies to ~10 µM even though it only has two connections to other P body components.
evidence: This is an observation that illustrates an exception to the connectivity rule.

claim: Xrn1's high concentration in P bodies is presumably due to the high affinity of the protein for RNA.
source: This is presumably due to the high affinity of the protein for RNA (Chang et al., 2011; Banani et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on known properties of Xrn1 and citations to previous literature.

claim: The exchange dynamics of Dhh1 appear to be governed by its rate of RNA-dependent ATP hydrolysis.
source: Finally, the exchange dynamics of Dhh1 appear to be governed by its rate of RNA-dependent ATP hydrolysis (Mugler et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: While connectivity patterns can be a useful guide to condensate composition and behavior, other molecular details must be considered to develop a complete understanding.
source: Thus, while connectivity patterns can be a useful guide to condensate composition and behavior, other molecular details must be considered to develop a complete understanding.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the limitations and utility of connectivity analysis.

claim: The positive correlations between HC protein concentrations suggest that these molecules partition into P bodies cooperatively.
source: The positive correlations between HC protein concentrations (Figure 3) suggest that these molecules partition into P bodies cooperatively.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed correlations.

claim: Cooperativity in HC protein partitioning likely arises from the high connectivity among the HC proteins.
source: This cooperativity likely arises from the high connectivity among the HC proteins, such that partitioning of one molecule promotes partitioning of others that interact with it directly and indirectly.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation for the observed cooperativity.

claim: Given the high concentration and multivalency of HC P body components, one would predict that they would all be able to contribute to P body assembly.
source: Given the high concentration and multivalency of HC P body components one would predict that they would all be able to contribute to P body assembly.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the properties of HC proteins.

claim: The three most enriched P body components, Dcp2, Pat1, and Edc3, are the three major proteins shown to affect P body assembly.
source: Indeed, this is what is seen in the literature. The three most enriched P body components, Dcp2, Pat1, and Edc3, are the three major proteins shown to affect P body assembly (Buchan et al., 2008; Decker et al., 2007; Teixeira and Parker, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous genetic studies.

claim: Other HC proteins, Dhh1, Upf1, and the Lsm1-7 complex can contribute to P body assembly.
source: Other HC proteins, Dhh1, Upf1, and the Lsm1-7 complex can contribute to P body assembly as well (Decker et al., 2007; Sheth and Parker, 2006; Hondele et al., 2019; Rao and Parker, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: None of the LC components are required for efficient P-body assembly.
source: In contrast, none of the LC components are required for efficient P-body assembly.
evidence: This is based on assessment of the genetic literature.

claim: Interactions that produce condensates are distributed across their highly-valent components.
source: This illustrates a second principle that interactions that produce condensates are distributed across their highly-valent components.
evidence: This is a general principle inferred from the observations.

claim: Highly-valent components act with differing degrees of cooperativity to promote formation of condensates.
source: These act with differing degrees of cooperativity to promote formation of the larger assembly.
evidence: This is a general principle inferred from the observations.

claim: This principle can explain why smaller P-bodies can still assemble in cells lacking one HC protein component.
source: This principle can explain why smaller P-bodies can still assemble in cells lacking one HC protein component (Rao and Parker, 2017).
evidence: This is an explanation for previous observations, supported by citation.

claim: In dcp1Δ strains, the HC components Dcp2:Edc3:Pat1:Lsm1:Dhh1:Xrn1 are present at roughly equimolar concentrations (~10 µM), with the exception of Upf1, which is ~2 fold lower.
source: It is notable that in the dcp1Δ strains, the HC components, Dcp2:Edc3:Pat1:Lsm1:Dhh1:Xrn1, are present at roughly equimolar concentrations (~10 µM), with the exception of Upf1, which is ~2 fold lower.
evidence: This is an observation from the quantitative data.

claim: The roughly equimolar concentrations of HC components suggest they might form a discrete, stoichiometrically defined RNP complex.
source: This suggests that perhaps these components form a discrete, stoichiometrically defined RNP complex which then assembles to higher order to form the condensate.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the equimolar concentrations.

claim: The data speak against HC proteins forming a strictly stoichiometric complex.
source: However, our data speak against this extreme of high cooperativity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple lines of evidence.

claim: The ratio of Dcp2 to Edc3 ranges from 0.5 to 2.3.
source: First, the ratio of Dcp2 to Edc3 ranges from 0.5 to 2.3 in our analysis, inconsistent with a strictly defined ratio expected from a stoichiometric complex on every mRNA.
evidence: This is an observation from the quantitative data that argues against strict stoichiometry.

claim: The cooperativity in P body concentrations is significant, but not as high as expected from a discrete complex.
source: Cast differently, the cooperativity in P body concentrations illustrated in Figure 3 is significant, but not as high as expected from a discrete complex.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the correlation data.

claim: The P body concentrations of Pat1 and the Lsm1-7 complex drop about two fold in wild type strains under glucose starvation relative to the dcp1Δ strains.
source: Further, the P body concentrations of Pat1 and the Lsm1-7 complex drop about two fold in wild type strains under glucose starvation conditions relative to the dcp1Δ strains, again speaking against a discrete assembly and suggesting that the interaction network of the HC proteins could be altered under different conditions.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing data under different conditions.

claim: The interaction network of HC proteins could be altered under different conditions.
source: Further, the P body concentrations of Pat1 and the Lsm1-7 complex drop about two fold in wild type strains under glucose starvation conditions relative to the dcp1Δ strains, again speaking against a discrete assembly and suggesting that the interaction network of the HC proteins could be altered under different conditions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed changes in protein concentrations under different conditions.

claim: Intermolecular RNA-RNA interactions may contribute to P body assembly.
source: An unanswered question is whether intermolecular RNA-RNA interactions contribute to P body assembly.
evidence: This identifies an open question in the field.

claim: The possibility of RNA-RNA interactions contributing to P body assembly is suggested by the robust self-assembly of RNA.
source: This possibility is suggested by the robust self-assembly of RNA, the roles of intermolecular RNA-RNA interactions in stress granule assembly (Van Treeck et al., 2018; Tauber et al., 2020), the observation that RNA is required for P body formation (Teixeira et al., 2005), and the fact that every P body protein interacts with RNA (Supplementary file 3 and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This speculation is supported by multiple lines of evidence from the literature.

claim: P body formation clearly requires protein interactions.
source: P body formation clearly requires protein interactions since Dcp2, Edc3, Dhh1, Lsm1-7 complex and Pat1 have all been genetically shown to promote P body formation (Decker et al., 2007; Teixeira and Parker, 2007; Rao and Parker, 2017; Hondele et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous genetic studies.

claim: The assembly of P bodies can be directly attributed to specific protein-protein interactions, such as the requirement for Edc3 dimerization.
source: In some cases, the assembly of P bodies can be directly attributed to specific protein-protein interactions, such as the requirement for Edc3 dimerization to promote P body formation (Ling et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Several P body proteins either in isolation, or in mixtures, can undergo LLPS to create P body like assemblies in vitro.
source: Moreover, several P body proteins either in isolation, or in mixtures, can undergo LLPS to create P body like assemblies in vitro (Fromm et al., 2014; Schütz et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous in vitro studies.

claim: Whether mRNAs in P bodies simply serve as a platform to facilitate interactions between HC P body components, or also form intermolecular RNA-RNA interactions contributing to P body formation remains to be seen.
source: Whether the mRNAs in P bodies simply serve as a platform to facilitate interactions between HC P body components, or also form intermolecular RNA-RNA interactions contributing to P body formation remains to be seen.
evidence: This identifies an open question about the role of RNA in P body assembly.

claim: Scaffolds are defined as components that are required for condensate formation.
source: Scaffolds are defined as components that are required for condensate formation, while clients are not necessary for integrity of the condensate, but are recruited by interacting with scaffolds.
evidence: This is a definition from a previously proposed model.

claim: Clients are not necessary for integrity of the condensate, but are recruited by interacting with scaffolds.
source: Scaffolds are defined as components that are required for condensate formation, while clients are not necessary for integrity of the condensate, but are recruited by interacting with scaffolds.
evidence: This is a definition from a previously proposed model.

claim: The scaffold/client model posited that there should generally be few scaffolds and many clients in natural condensates.
source: As corollaries, the model posited that there should generally be few scaffolds and many clients in natural condensates, and that scaffolds should have high valency of interaction elements, while clients should have lower valency.
evidence: This describes predictions from a previously proposed model.

claim: The scaffold/client model posited that scaffolds should have high valency of interaction elements, while clients should have lower valency.
source: As corollaries, the model posited that there should generally be few scaffolds and many clients in natural condensates, and that scaffolds should have high valency of interaction elements, while clients should have lower valency.
evidence: This describes predictions from a previously proposed model.

claim: The scaffold/client model posited that scaffolds should have higher concentration within the condensate than clients.
source: In addition, scaffolds should have higher concentration within the condensate than clients, since the former recruit the latter.
evidence: This describes a prediction from a previously proposed model.

claim: The yeast P body scaffolds include RNA as well as Dcp2, Edc3, Pat1, Lsm1-7 and Dhh1.
source: In this view, the yeast P body scaffolds include RNA (Teixeira et al., 2005) as well as Dcp2, Edc3, and Pat1, Lsm1-7 and Dhh1 (Decker et al., 2007; Teixeira and Parker, 2007; Hondele et al., 2019), since deletion of these factors impairs formation of the condensate.
evidence: This classification is based on genetic studies showing these components are required for P body formation.

claim: All yeast P body scaffold proteins are in the HC group and have high valency of interaction and high connectivity.
source: Notably, all of these proteins are in the HC group and have high valency of interaction and high connectivity.
evidence: This is an observation connecting the scaffold classification with the HC group.

claim: No molecules in the LC group are known to impair P body formation under the conditions tested.
source: Under the same conditions, no molecules in the LC group are known to impair P body formation (although when cells are at high density, deletion of Sbp1 produces smaller P bodies [Segal et al., 2006]).
evidence: This is based on assessment of the genetic literature.

claim: Information on the relative concentrations of proteins in a condensate (the HC vs LC distinction) is likely to aid prediction of molecules that play significant roles in generating the structure.
source: Thus, information on the relative concentrations of proteins in a condensate (the HC vs LC distinction) is likely to aid prediction of molecules that play significant roles in generating the structure (and be imperfectly correlated with connectivity, as described above).
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of concentration measurements for predicting function.

claim: A simple scaffold/client classification does not account for the differences in effect of various deletions.
source: Yet a simple scaffold/client classification does not account for the differences in effect of the various deletions; for example loss of RNA completely eliminates P bodies, whereas loss of the other factors has only a partial effect.
evidence: This identifies a limitation of the simple scaffold/client model.

claim: Scaffold and client are better used as descriptors rather than a black-and-white classification.
source: Thus, rather than a black-and-white classification, we have come to believe that scaffold and client are better used as descriptors, where condensate components are more scaffold-like or more client-like depending on the degree to which their deletion affects the cooperative assembly of other components.
evidence: This is a refinement of the scaffold/client model based on the observations.

claim: Scaffold-like components contribute more strongly to condensate formation; their deletion should decrease the size and number of condensates.
source: Scaffold-like components contribute more strongly to condensate formation; their deletion should decrease the size and number of condensates.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the refined scaffold/client model.

claim: Client-like components should have lesser or no effects on condensate size and number upon deletion.
source: Client-like components should have lesser or no such effects.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the refined scaffold/client model.

claim: Scaffold-like components should have higher connectivity among molecules in the condensate and be more central in the interaction network.
source: Intuitively, scaffold-like components should have higher connectivity among molecules in the condensate, and will be more central in the interaction network, whereas client-like molecules should have low connectivity and be more peripheral in the network.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the refined scaffold/client model.

claim: Client-like molecules should have low connectivity and be more peripheral in the interaction network.
source: Intuitively, scaffold-like components should have higher connectivity among molecules in the condensate, and will be more central in the interaction network, whereas client-like molecules should have low connectivity and be more peripheral in the network.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the refined scaffold/client model.

claim: A similar concept of scaffold-like and client-like components has been described in the context of stress granules recently.
source: A similar concept has been described in the context of stress granules recently (Yang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a recent study.

claim: Highly connected molecules are expected to have greater influence on the composition of condensates.
source: In addition to affecting formation of the condensate, highly connected molecules are expected to have greater influence on the composition of the structure.
evidence: This is a prediction based on principles of network connectivity.

claim: Deletion of scaffold-like molecules will change partitioning of numerous components.
source: Deletion of scaffold-like molecules will change partitioning of numerous components, while deletion of client-like molecules will only affect partitioning of their immediate interacting components in the network.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the refined scaffold/client model.

claim: Deletion of client-like molecules will only affect partitioning of their immediate interacting components in the network.
source: Deletion of scaffold-like molecules will change partitioning of numerous components, while deletion of client-like molecules will only affect partitioning of their immediate interacting components in the network.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the refined scaffold/client model.

claim: Deleting molecules is likely to have heterogeneous effects on condensate composition, changing the relative ratios of components.
source: Importantly, since connectivity in a condensate is not homogeneous (different molecules have different connectivity), deleting molecules is likely to have heterogeneous effects on composition, changing the relative ratios of components.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the heterogeneity of connectivity.

claim: The thermodynamics of forming a condensate and the composition of the resulting structure will be coupled, based on the connectivity patterns in the interaction network.
source: Thus, the thermodynamics of forming a condensate and the composition of the resulting structure will be coupled, based on the connectivity patterns in the interaction network.
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion about the relationship between thermodynamics and composition.

claim: Further exploration of scaffold/client ideas will require large-scale, systematic analysis of condensate composition in the presence of individual deletions of multiple components.
source: Further exploration of these ideas will require large-scale, systematic analysis of condensate composition in the presence of individual deletions of multiple components.
evidence: This identifies future experimental directions.

claim: Simple mass action will concentrate components that bind with high affinity to scaffolds.
source: First, simple mass action will concentrate components that bind with high affinity to scaffolds.
evidence: This is a general principle of biochemistry applied to condensates.

claim: High affinity binding to RNA likely explains the strong partitioning of Xrn1 into P bodies.
source: High affinity binding to RNA likely also explains the strong partitioning of Xrn1 into P bodies, even though it makes few known interactions with other components and its loss does not have deleterious effects to formation of the condensates (i.e. it is more client-like than scaffold-like in its properties).
evidence: This is an inference based on the properties of Xrn1.

claim: Increasing affinity for a condensate component does not increase partitioning if affinity is already high.
source: Second, increasing affinity for a condensate component does not increase partitioning if affinity is already high.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experiments with Dcp2 FL-H1.

claim: The upper bound of partitioning may be determined by limiting concentrations of scaffold-like interaction partners.
source: The upper bound may be determined by limiting concentrations of scaffold-like interaction partners.
evidence: This is an inference about what limits partitioning.

claim: Partitioning may be more readily tuned when it is mediated by weak multivalent interactions rather than by high affinity interactions.
source: This also indicates that partitioning may be more readily tuned when it is mediated by weak multivalent interactions rather than by high affinity interactions.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the tunability of partitioning based on the observations.

claim: Protein elements that bind scaffold-like components weakly will not partition strongly into a condensate individually.
source: Third, protein elements that bind scaffold-like components weakly will not partition strongly into a condensate, but when two such elements are fused together, even if they bind different scaffold-like components, they can be recruited strongly.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experiments with Dcp2 fragments.

claim: When two weak-binding elements are fused together, even if they bind different scaffold-like components, they can be recruited strongly into a condensate.
source: Third, protein elements that bind scaffold-like components weakly will not partition strongly into a condensate, but when two such elements are fused together, even if they bind different scaffold-like components, they can be recruited strongly.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experiments with Dcp2 fragments.

claim: Cooperativity between IDRs and folded domains can promote recruitment into both phase separated droplets in vitro and P bodies in cells.
source: This behavior is analogous to previous observations that cooperativity between IDRs and folded domains can promote recruitment into both phase separated droplets in vitro and P bodies in cells (Lin et al., 2015; Protter et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Synergistic effects between weak binding elements will greatly narrow the specificity of recruitment.
source: Such effects, similar to avidity effects in canonical molecular interactions, will greatly narrow the specificity of recruitment, even for scaffolds that individually bind ligands promiscuously.
evidence: This is a conclusion about how synergy affects specificity.

claim: This mechanism provides ready routes for evolution of new clients through genetic rearrangements that fuse together multiple low-affinity interaction elements.
source: This mechanism also provides ready routes for evolution of new clients through genetic rearrangements that fuse together multiple low-affinity interaction elements.
evidence: This is a speculation about evolutionary implications.

claim: Distributing recruitment across a large number of interaction elements would render composition less susceptible to mutations, which could lead to evolutionary selection.
source: Distributing recruitment across a large number of interaction elements would also render composition less susceptible to mutations, which could lead to evolutionary selection.
evidence: This is a speculation about evolutionary implications.

claim: A similar mechanism may be applied to RNA partitioning, since a predominant metric for mRNA partitioning into P bodies or stress granules is length.
source: A similar mechanism may be applied to RNA partitioning as well, since a predominant metric for mRNA partitioning into P bodies or stress granules is length, which may be a simple proxy for the number for interactions (Khong et al., 2017; Matheny et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by citations to previous studies on RNA partitioning.

claim: mRNA length may be a simple proxy for the number of interactions in condensate partitioning.
source: A similar mechanism may be applied to RNA partitioning as well, since a predominant metric for mRNA partitioning into P bodies or stress granules is length, which may be a simple proxy for the number for interactions (Khong et al., 2017; Matheny et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Several condensates, including P bodies, have been proposed as sites for sequestration/storage of biomolecules.
source: For example, several condensates, including P bodies, have been proposed as sites for sequestration/storage of biomolecules, in part because they appear as qualitatively bright puncta by microscopy, and in part because their disruption can activate certain processes (Arimoto et al., 2008; Decker and Parker, 2012; Li et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: When total condensate volume and partition coefficients are quantified, it is evident that only a small fraction of most molecular species are sequestered within condensates.
source: However, when total condensate volume (typically <1–2% of cytoplasm/nucleoplasm), and partition coefficients (2 ~ 200) are quantified, it is evident that only a small fraction of most molecular species are sequestered within condensates. (Figure 4, Leung et al., 2006; Rao and Parker, 2017; Wheeler et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on quantitative measurements in this study and citations to previous studies.

claim: In some processes, small changes in the amount of available species in the cytoplasm/nucleoplasm could have functional consequences.
source: While in some processes small changes in the amount of available species in the cytoplasm/nucleoplasm could have functional consequences, in others, different mechanisms must be considered.
evidence: This acknowledges that even small changes could be functionally relevant in some cases.

claim: An inhibitory catalytic function within a condensate could explain the activation of a process upon condensate disruption, rather than sequestration.
source: For example, rather than sequestration, an inhibitory catalytic function within a condensate could also explain the activation of a process upon condensate disruption.
evidence: This proposes an alternative mechanism to sequestration.

claim: Condensates may generally be organized around a relatively small number of highly concentrated, less dynamic scaffold-like components.
source: Together, our work suggests that condensates may generally be organized around a relatively small number of highly concentrated, less dynamic scaffold-like components.
evidence: This is a general conclusion based on the P body data.

claim: A condensate organized around a small number of scaffold-like components would provide a relatively simple route for appearance during evolution.
source: This construction would provide a relatively simple route for a condensate to appear during evolution, in that only a small number of proteins would need to develop the ability to assemble cooperatively.
evidence: This is a speculation about evolutionary implications.

claim: Once a condensate structure is established, other proteins could evolve the ability to interact with scaffold-like components and be recruited into the compartment to different degrees.
source: Once this structure was established, other proteins could evolve the ability to interact with the scaffold-like components and consequently be recruited into the compartment to different degrees determined by their connectivity, interaction affinity and cooperativity among different interaction elements.
evidence: This is a speculation about evolutionary mechanisms.

claim: Condensates are compositionally less complicated than suggested by proteomics studies.
source: A composition of this nature also indicates that condensates are compositionally less complicated than suggested by proteomics studies, where tens to hundreds of proteins have been annotated as residents of particular condensates.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the quantitative data showing only a few highly concentrated proteins.

claim: Most condensate components are present in only small amounts, and the majority of the protein mass derives from only a few types of molecules.
source: Our quantitation indicates that most components are present in only small amounts, and the majority of the protein mass derives from only a few types of molecules.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the quantitative data.

claim: Understanding that condensates are compositionally simpler greatly simplifies efforts to reconstitute condensates in vitro.
source: Such an understanding greatly simplifies efforts to reconstitute condensates in vitro, and can frame models of their biochemical functions.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the practical implications of the findings.
